Topics · Is there a God?

Is anyone really listening, or is it a feeling?

A feeling cannot settle this alone. Tests for your own life, and the Quran's first-person sentence: I am near.

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:186

Translation

Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 145:18

World English Bible

A feeling happens inside you, so by itself it cannot prove that anyone else is there. It cannot disprove it either. What separates a feeling from a presence is what follows. A mood fades and leaves nothing. A reply, if there is one, shows up afterwards: in what steadies you, in what you find yourself able to do, in what comes to you unasked. The verse makes one claim in the first person, and it is a claim you can check against your own life.

A question for you

Which test would you trust most?

If you sayWhat it does to my life afterwards
ThenThat is a fair test, and it is the one the verse leans on. It speaks of a call being answered and of finding one's way, and both are things you can look for after the moment has passed.
If you sayWhether it comes when I am not trying
ThenReasonable. A feeling you produce on purpose proves little, because you are the author of it. What arrives unasked, and what asks something of you in return, deserves more of your attention.
If you sayI do not think I could tell
ThenThat is an honest place to stand. You can leave the question open and still look, slowly. Nothing in the next steps asks you to decide today.

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ ۖ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have already created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer[1528] to him than [his] jugular vein.

Translator's notes

[1528] In absolute knowledge of everything about him. "We" has also been interpreted to mean the angels who are mentioned in the following verse.

Quran · Qaf 50:16

Translation

You are near, Yahweh. All your commandments are truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וְֽכָל־מִצְוֺתֶ֥יךָ אֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 119:151

World English Bible

Any answer to your question has to deal with distance first. How could anything hear a thought you never said aloud? The verse answers with the nearest thing it can name, your own pulse, and says closer than that. It adds that the one speaking knows what the self whispers to itself. If that is so, the question changes shape. It is no longer whether someone is near enough to hear. It is how such nearness could be noticed at all.

A question for you

When you sit in silence, where does the other end of it seem to be?

If you sayFar away
ThenThen your feeling and the verse give different distances, and that is worth knowing. It is worth testing which of the two holds up.
If you sayClose, inside me
ThenThat fits the verse. Notice what it adds: the nearness it names is to you, measured on your own body, not only a place within you. Whether that difference matters is yours to decide.
If you sayNowhere I can find
ThenThen say so, and keep looking. The verse does not ask you to pretend a nearness you do not feel. It makes a claim and leaves the checking to you.

Part 3 of 4

﴿أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Is He [not best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth?[1084] Is there a deity with Allāh? Little do you remember.

Translator's notes

[1084] Generation after generation.

Quran · An-Naml 27:62

Translation

For who is God, except Yahweh? Who is a rock, besides our God,

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֤י מִ֣י אֱ֭לוֹהַּ מִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וּמִ֥י צ֝֗וּר זוּלָתִ֥י אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

the Psalms · 18:31

World English Bible

Here is a test that needs no belief in advance, only memory. Think of the worst hour you have had, when every plan had failed and nobody could reach you. What did you do? Many people who would never use the word find themselves asking, without choosing to, for help from beyond anything in the room. The verse asks who answers someone in that position, and who lifts the harm. It does not supply the answer. It asks the question.

A question for you

Think of a time you ran out of options. What did you do first?

If you sayI called out, in words or without them
ThenThat is the experience the verse relies on. It does not claim that this proves someone heard. It asks what you were reaching for, and leaves the answer to you.
If you sayI went quiet and endured
ThenEndurance is a real response. The verse speaks of those who call; it does not measure those who held on in silence.
If you sayI turned to people
ThenOf course. People are the first help, and often the way help arrives. The verse asks only about what is left when people cannot reach you.
If you sayI have never been there
ThenThen this test is not yet yours to run, and it would be unfair to make you run it. The next verse offers a different way in.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُوا۟ فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways.[1136] And indeed, Allāh is with the doers of good.

Translator's notes

[1136] The various ways and means to attain the acceptance and pleasure of Allāh.

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:69

Translation

But from there you shall seek Yahweh your God, and you will find him when you search after him with all your heart and with all your soul.

Original · Hebrew

וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּ֥ם מִשָּׁ֛ם אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וּמָצָ֑אתָ כִּ֣י תִדְרְשֶׁ֔נּוּ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 4:29

World English Bible

What if you do all this honestly and feel nothing? The verse speaks to that reader too, and it is careful in what it promises. It speaks of those who strive for God: they will be guided to His ways, and God is with those who do good. Striving is something you can do without feeling anything. The promise is about direction, not about a sensation, and it names no date.

A question for you

If nothing has come, what would you want to try?

If you sayKeep looking, slowly
ThenSlow is allowed. The verse sets no deadline, and a pace you can keep is better than a burst you cannot.
If you sayAsk plainly, in my own words
ThenThat is what the first verse describes: a call, in whatever words you have. It does not need to be polished.
If you sayRest for now
ThenRest is not failure. The questions will still be here, and so will you.

The same in the other books

Translation

‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and will show you great and difficult things, which you don’t know.’

Original · Hebrew

קְרָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וְאֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ וְאַגִּ֧ידָה לְּךָ֛ גְּדֹל֥וֹת וּבְצֻר֖וֹת לֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽם׃

Jeremiah · 33:3

World English Bible

Translation

Call on me in the day of trouble. I will deliver you, and you will honor me.”

Original · Hebrew

וּ֭קְרָאֵנִי בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה אֲ֝חַלֶּצְךָ֗ וּֽתְכַבְּדֵֽנִי׃

the Psalms · 50:15

World English Bible

Translation

“Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you. For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.

Original · Ancient Greek

Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν. πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 7:7-8

World English Bible

Translation

If you take advantage of them at all, and they cry at all to me, I will surely hear their cry;

Original · Hebrew

אִם־עַנֵּ֥ה תְעַנֶּ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י אִם־צָעֹ֤ק יִצְעַק֙ אֵלַ֔י שָׁמֹ֥עַ אֶשְׁמַ֖ע צַעֲקָתֽוֹ׃

the Torah (Exodus) · 22:23

World English Bible

All the matching texts: God, near and merciful

Your reflection

Think of the moment you have felt most connected. What did you do the day after? What does that say about whether it was only a feeling?
